statement: For 2D rectangular knapsack, a contact-point placement heuristic (scoring free rectangles by total edge length touching bin walls) reduces interior fragmentation and improves packing profit by ~0.5% compared to BSSF/BAF/BL alone.
regime: Bins 900-2000 with 8-12 item types; most effective when bin dimensions are near-prime and items have diverse aspect ratios
mechanism: CP scoring pushes items toward bin walls, creating larger contiguous interior spaces rather than scattered fragments. This is especially helpful when no item dimension evenly divides the bin dimension.
applicability_bounds: Effect is small (~0.5 points); may not manifest on bins with dimensions that are multiples of common item sizes

statement: Bin transposition (packing in H×W instead of W×H, then translating coordinates) consistently finds better solutions on ~20-30% of test cases, because the BL heuristic's bottom-left bias interacts differently with the bin's aspect ratio.
regime: Most effective when W != H; no benefit when bin is square
mechanism: The BL heuristic fills from (0,0) upward and rightward. In a W×H bin vs H×W bin, items encounter different free-rect geometries at each step. Transposition is equivalent to rotating the bin 90°, which changes which dimension 'fills first'.
applicability_bounds: Only useful for non-square bins; adds constant overhead of duplicating packing runs

statement: Both-orientation best-fit (trying both rotations and picking the tighter fit) is far superior to fallback rotation (try unrotated, rotate only if it doesn't fit). The improvement is ~6 points on the judge scoring formula.
regime: Any 2D knapsack with rotation allowed; the largest single improvement found in this campaign
mechanism: Fallback rotation commits to the unrotated orientation even when the rotated version produces a tighter fit with less wasted space. Best-fit rotation evaluates both and picks the one minimizing the heuristic score, leading to consistently less fragmentation.
applicability_bounds: No effect when allow_rotate=false or when w==h for all types
